title: Can Fintech Development Contribute to Mitigating the Greenhouse Effect? A Global Perspective
technology: Fintech development (World Bank Fintech activity index, 3 subindices: equity investment in Fintech firms, online Fintech credit, digital payments via mobile/internet)
estimator: Cross-sectional OLS, log-log; Lewbel 2SLS and external-instrument IV as endogeneity check; income-group models estimated separately

contrasts.study: Can Fintech Development Contribute to Mitigating the Greenhouse Effect? A Global Perspective
contrasts.outcome: GHG emissions (MtCO2e, log); CO2 in robustness
contrasts.poorer_group: low- and lower-middle-income (combined by the authors)
contrasts.p_rich: significant, exact value not in extraction
contrasts.p_poor: significant, exact value not in extraction
contrasts.evidence: Table III, models (2) and (4), journal pp. 1836-1837: 'Fintech development significantly reduces GHGEs in low- and lower-middle-income countries and high-income countries, but this effect is insignificant in upper-middle-income countries.' PDF page not determined.
contrasts.notes: Outcome is GHG emissions; lower is better, so the sign is reversed and benefit is coded as a more negative coefficient. Table III coefficients and SEs are not in the extracted text (only the title and layout survive), so b, SE, t and N are null. Both groups are significant reductions; no formal difference test is reported in the text, so direction is unclear. Richest vs poorest pair per headline rule: high vs low+lower-middle (combined). Count of economies: low-income = 15 countries (text); combined group size and per-group N not stated, so null. Total sample 124 countries, cross-section.

title: The Role of ICTs on Innovation Process of Environment and Energy Convergence
technology: ICT usage (mobile cellular subscriptions and internet users; the paper labels this variable 'innovation')
estimator: Absolute and conditional beta-convergence with lagged dependent variable; pooled OLS and panel quantile regression

contrasts.study: The Role of ICTs on Innovation Process of Environment and Energy Convergence
contrasts.outcome: Growth of per capita CO2 emissions (log difference; conditional convergence)
contrasts.estimator: Conditional beta-convergence, panel quantile regression (25th, 50th, 75th) and pooled OLS
contrasts.evidence: Rendered Table VII (journal p. 4430), panel OLS column: MCS lower-middle -1.20 (0.012), Obs 420; low income -0.120 (0.023), Obs 770.
contrasts.notes: Outcome is a growth rate of CO2; lower emissions is the benefit, so sign reversed for benefit coding. The ICT coefficients for the LMI and LI columns are in Table VII, which is not present in the extracted text (blank table body), so all numbers are null. The text gives the ICT effect only for the full sample (insignificant). Its statements on LMI and LI concern institutional quality and GDP, not ICT. Direction unclear. Group sizes not stated. Only pair available (LMI vs LI), so headline. Judgement: outcome family 6 because CO2 is named in the family definition; ICT measure is mobile and internet use, so exposure is eligible. Implausible: coefficients with t above 50 carry no significance stars; the full-sample MCS is -1.328 (0.001) without stars. Flagged. Checked by the lead analyst.

contrasts.study: The Role of ICTs on Innovation Process of Environment and Energy Convergence
contrasts.outcome: Growth of per capita energy consumption (log difference; conditional convergence)
contrasts.estimator: Conditional beta-convergence, panel quantile regression and pooled OLS
contrasts.evidence: Table IX (journal p. 4433), text on pp. 4434: the ICT effect on energy consumption is described for the full sample ('substantial role of innovation through ICT for energy consumption').
contrasts.notes: Non-headline. Outcome is per capita energy use (kg oil equivalent), coded as family 6 as resource cost; the family definition names electricity use, so this is a judgement call. The ICT coefficient by group is not in the extracted text. Energy use: higher is a cost, so benefit coding reverses sign. Absolute convergence split by group is in Table VI (p. 4429) and is not coded separately. Forestry area (Tables V and VIII) is not one of the six families, so not coded.
